metadata.description: read-heavy product recommendations: concurrent read scaling under a production-shaped read/write MIX (paired control vs mixed arms)

notes: CONCURRENCY LADDER (read-heavy MIX, 8 rungs × 2 arm(s) over 1,2,4,8 against 'recodb'): the headline evidence is where throughput SATURATES while latency explodes and only a subset of cores stay busy — the single-engine-thread vs off-thread-reader-pool signature — measured under a PRODUCTION-SHAPED MIX (reads served while writes commit underneath), not against a frozen graph.

TWO LAYERS OF TRUTH, never conflated (rmp #714, #715). READ: throughput.* is ONE coherent set — the 1498 reads of the best 'mixed' rung (C=8), at 717.3 ops/s, and throughput.abort_rate = 0.000000 is the READ abort rate. It is a MEASURED zero, not a placeholder: a standalone auto-commit read runs at SNAPSHOT ISOLATION (rmp #543/#545), so it can neither abort a writer nor be aborted by one — that is invariant I1, and the run FAILS if a read ever aborts. WRITE: the writers' evidence lives in the workload map and is split in two. ENGINE: 0 of 1752 transaction attempts were aborted by SSI (engine_abort_rate 0.000000). APPLICATION: 1752 of 1752 business units COMMITTED (write_commit_rate 1.000000), at 0.0000 retries per commit, 0 exhausting their retry budget. A high engine abort rate WITH a full application commit rate is a HEALTHY system under contention: the application-visible cost of contention is LATENCY (see write_p99_ms, which is RETRY-INCLUSIVE), not lost work.

THE COST OF THE MIX (rmp #714). Every rung was run TWICE, back to back, same concurrency, same op budget, same graph: once with the writers OFF (the control) and once with them ON (the treatment — the production-shaped default this report headlines). What the mix costs the READ path: -8.0% at the best rung (C=8). Rung by rung: C=1: 196.5 → 186.9 ops/s (-4.9%), p99 31.2 → 31.5 ms | C=2: 384.2 → 368.1 ops/s (-4.2%), p99 32.1 → 32.5 ms | C=4: 576.2 → 551.3 ops/s (-4.3%), p99 45.3 → 44.6 ms | C=8: 779.9 → 717.3 ops/s (-8.0%), p99 75.8 → 75.6 ms. The control arm runs FIRST at every rung, so it warms the buffer pool for the mixed arm — the cost reported here is therefore a conservative LOWER BOUND. This is the number a capacity planner needs and that a read-only ladder against a frozen graph can never produce.

THE WRITE STREAM is production-shaped, not a storm: 2 writer(s) paced at one business unit every 20ms, each driven through MANAGED RETRY (bounded exponential backoff + jitter — what session.execute_write does in every official driver). 25% of the units are a read-modify-write of one of 4 TRENDING products (`SET p.hot = coalesce(p.hot,0)+1`); the rest CREATE a PURCHASED edge on a random (user, product) pair. The hot component is what makes SSI — and therefore the retry path — LOAD-BEARING: a purely random write stream conflicts with nobody, aborts nothing, and leaves the retry path as dead code and the bounded-retries invariant vacuous.

SLOW-READER PROBE (invariant I5, the GC pin — rmp #551): while 107 heavy 'r3_fof3' traversals (p50 22.8ms, max 57.1ms) held their MVCC snapshots open for 3.0s, the writers committed 263 of 263 business units underneath them (0 engine aborts). A long reader pins the GC watermark; if that pin could stall the write path, this window would show ZERO commits — and the ladder, whose reads are all short, would never have noticed.

storage.bytes_fsynced is a proxy: the WAL on-disk byte count (every committed WAL byte is fsynced before commit acknowledgement), not a directly-observed fsync counter.

storage.bytes_per_node / bytes_per_relationship are deliberately ABSENT (rmp #711/#714): the dataset counts are the GENERATOR's seed graph, while the mixed arm COMMITTED 1752 business unit(s) into this same store — most of them a CREATE of a new PURCHASED edge. The store therefore no longer holds the graph those counts describe, and a per-element cost computed from them would be real arithmetic over the wrong graph.

storage.* is the REAL on-disk footprint of the 'recodb' database after the ladder: a 6922240 B store image plus a 7360747 B WAL DIRECTORY of segment files (walked by PATH). The amplification ratios are those durable bytes over the generator's 2433133 B logical CSV — and they now include the durable cost of the writes the mix committed, so they are an UPPER bound on the load's own amplification.

KNEE: VERDICT: reads SCALED ACROSS CORES — 33 threads were busy and total core usage reached 12.10, well above any single thread's 0.75. The read path spread work across cores (the off-thread reader pool #336/#527 is engaged).
KNEE: Server disk read IO at the top rung: 0.0 MiB over the rung (reads are largely served from the buffer pool when this stays low).
